learning_outcomes:
RELS 1.  |  Major programme:
Knowledge: Graduates will have acquired the
following:
(1)  |  The
understanding of religion in its historical settings and contemporary
contexts of modern living, globally and locally.
(2)  |  The
understanding of religion in its different dimensions.
(3)  |  The
understanding of religion through a crtical analysis.
(4)  |  A
basic knowledge of major religious traditions in the world.
Skills: Graduates will have acquired the
following:
(1)  |  Communication
and presentational (oral and written) skills.
(2)  |  Analytical
and problem solving skills.
(3)  |  Social
skills and team-work skills.
(4)  |  Skills
of critical intelligence and appreciative thinking.
(5)  |  Skills
in cross-cultural understanding and intercultural literacy.
(6)  |  Research
skills.
Attitude: Graduates will have acquired the
following:
(1)  |  Awareness
of the plurality and multi-faceted complexity within religious traditions of
the issues of multiple and conflicting interpretations of religious
traditions.
(2)  |  Self-critical
awareness of pre-suppositions and recognition.
(3)  |  A
critical and yet sympathetic understanding and appreciation of religious
traditions especially those to which one does not belong.
(4)  |  Sensitivity
to the ultimate concern and the religious dimension of human life.
2.  |  Minor programme:
i.  |  Arab Studies
Upon completion of the programme,
students will have acquired the following learning outcomes in three aspects: I. Knowledge outcomes: (1) Understand religions and cultures of the Arab
World in their historical settings and contemporary contexts of modern
living. (2) Recognize central themes and issues in the
Arab World, especially with respect to cultural and religious dimensions. II. Skills outcomes: (1) Basic command of the Arabic language. (2) Engage in a critical analysis of issues
pertaining to the Arab World by the methods of the humanities and social
sciences. III. Attitude outcomes: (1) Have awareness of
plurality and multi-faceted complexity within Arab cultural, political and
religious traditions, and of the issues of multiple and conflicting
interpretations of language and symbols, texts and traditions. (2) Acknowledge the contested
and provisional nature of knowledge and understanding. Show tolerance of
diverse positions and have respect for others’ views.
ii.  |  Religious Studies
Upon the completion of the
Minor programme, students will have demonstrated basic understanding of
fundamental issues related to the subject, acquired knowledge of some aspects
of the subject with sufficient exposure and at a suitable level to allow
further study in this subject or related subjects or to pursue a related
career.
iii. Religion
and Health Upon
completion of this Minor Programme, students will have acquired the ability
to: I.
Knowledge outcomes: a) gain a comprehensive
understanding of the relationship between religion and health, including the
impact of religion (e.g. belief/ritual/practice) on physical, mental, and spiritual
well-being, within their cultural and historical contexts. b) analyze how religion
influences health behaviours, healthcare decision-making, and attitudes
towards illness and healing. c) identify and utilize
resources and practices that promote spiritually informed self-care from
diverse perspectives. II.
Skills outcomes: a) design health
programmes that incorporate religious resources, such as texts, rituals, or
practices, to enhance the well-being of individuals and communities. b) demonstrate
proficiency in conducting research and data analysis related to religion and
health. c) effectively
communicate findings to diverse audiences, including healthcare
professionals, community stakeholders and policymakers. III.
Values and attitude outcomes: a) foster cultural
sensitivity and respect for the clients’ religious beliefs and practices in
healthcare settings. b) increase awareness
of the impact of religious resources on population health in different parts
of our global communities. c) engage in ongoing
education and dialogue to deepen understanding of the intersection between
spirituality, healthcare ethics, and diverse religious traditions.
